text:
[verdict]
In the 50 retrieved historical episodes where the tape looked like TSLA on 2026-09-18, the median realised return over the next 20 sessions was 2.96%, with a mean of 2.39%. The distribution is slightly left-skewed at -0.288, meaning the downside tail is thicker than the upside, and 32% of those analogs finished below zero. The single number to anchor on for path risk is the median max adverse excursion of -3.53%, which shows how far these trades typically went underwater before the 20-session horizon closed.

[state]
The engine pulled these 50 analogs from 39 distinct sessions across 30 symbols because the current feature vector has a specific shape. TSLA is sitting 26.98% off its 52-week high (z-score -0.841) and in a 14.35% drawdown from its 60-session peak (z-score -0.749). Its 20-session realised volatility is elevated at 48.97% (z-score 0.983), yet the 5d/20d volatility ratio is compressed to 0.489 (z-score -1.217), indicating recent price action has been unusually quiet relative to the trailing month. Dollar volume is thin, with a 20-session dollar-volume regime z-score of -1.558 (used as -1.026). Macro context includes a WTI crude change over 20 days of 19.24% (z-score 1.124) and benchmark 20-session volatility at 9.16% (z-score -0.574). The event calendar is capped at 45 days to next earnings (z-score 0.663). These features collectively weight the retrieval toward names that were volatile but recently compressing, trading on low volume, and sitting well off highs. Only 1 of the 50 returned analogs is TSLA itself; the rest are drawn heavily from Technology (12), ETF China (8), China ADR (7), Consumer Disc. (5), and Health Care (5).

[history]
Over the 20-session horizon, the 50 analogs produced a median forward return of 2.96% and a standard deviation of 6.9%. The 10th percentile was -8.68% and the 90th percentile was 10.51%. The full range stretched from -11.47% to 15.49%. In 68% of the cases the return was above zero, and in 32% it was below. The bad tail is dominated by China ADR names: Li Auto (LI) on 2025-09-22 realised -11.47%, and Alibaba (BABA) on 2025-07-01 realised 2.99% but suffered a -9% max adverse excursion along the way. On the positive side, Schlumberger (SLB) on 2026-08-04 returned 12.48%, Nike (NKE) on 2023-10-10 returned 12.03%, and the single TSLA analog from 2025-08-07 returned 8.87%. The conformal interval, scaled at 1.768 and fitted on 2019-2022 data, spans from -9.24% to 15.15%, a total width of 24.38%. Out of sample from 2023 onward, this interval covered 87.4% of realised outcomes across 2627 test queries.

[tails]
Endpoint returns hide the intra-horizon pain. Across the 50 analogs, the median max adverse excursion was -3.53%. The 25th percentile of max adverse excursion was -7.38%, and the 10th percentile was -10.99%. Looking at breach probabilities, 40% of the analogs experienced a 5% drawdown at some point during the 20 sessions, and 14% breached a 10% drawdown. No analog in this set breached a 15% or 20% drawdown. The median max favourable excursion was 6.73%, with the 75th percentile at 9.45% and the 90th percentile at 14.07%. This yields a historical reward-to-risk ratio of 1.91 based on the median excursions.

[stress]
The stress scenarios that materially worsen the baseline median of 2.39% are led by rate and inflation regimes. Under the 2022 inflation / rate bear scenario, the median forward return drops to -7.83%, a delta of -10.79% versus baseline, with a 74% probability of breaching a 10% drawdown. The caveat is that this nine-month window means the per-date cap of 2 analogs samples it repeatedly; treat it as a regime description, not 50 independent events. The 2018-Q4 tightening scare produces a median of -6.29% (delta -9.25%), with a 50% probability of a 10% drawdown. Its caveat is that it ended with a policy pivot in January 2019, which flatters the forward returns of late-window analogs. The 2020-02/03 liquidity crash yields a median of -3.2% (delta -6.16%), but the 10th percentile plunges to -30.58% and the probability of a 10% drawdown hits 72.9%. The caveat is that central-bank backstops arrived inside the window, so the realised rebound is baked into the forward returns; it is a sample of one regime, not a forecast. The 2025-04 tariff shock gives a median of -0.86% (delta -3.82%) with a 61.5% probability of a 10% drawdown, carrying the caveat that policy reversals inside the window make the tail asymmetric in a way specific to that episode. The 2024-08-05 carry unwind shows a median of -0.03% (delta -2.99%), but the caveat notes the reversal was almost as fast as the drawdown, so H-day forward returns look benign even though the intra-horizon excursion did not. Among shocks, a +2 sigma VIX spike drops the median to -2.28% (delta -5.24%), with the caveat that VIX shocks mean-revert quickly, stressing entry timing more than terminal value. Earnings release day conditioning yields a median of -1.18% (delta -4.14%), with the caveat that earnings dates for foreign private issuers come from 6-K full-text search and are noisier than 8-K Item 2.02 dates. Crypto drawdown contagion gives a median of -1.99% (delta -4.95%), with the caveat that the BTC feature is a market-wide regime proxy and any name-level linkage to crypto flows is not identified here. Scenarios that did not severely worsen the picture include the 2023-03 regional bank stress (median 3.07%, delta 0.11%), whose caveat is that it is a very short window dominated by a handful of sessions; FOMC decision day (median 1.7%, delta -1.26%), caveated that only 92 decision days exist so the analog set is small and highly overlapping; China ADR de-rating (median 1%, delta -1.96%), caveated that delisting and audit-access risks are structural and will not appear in a price/vol feature space; policy-rate path re-pricing (median -0.66%, delta -3.62%), caveated that transmission depends on duration and balance sheet which are not features here; and liquidity air pocket (median 0.13%, delta -2.83%), caveated that gap20 is measured on the underlying exchange session, bounding reference-market gap risk only. No scenarios had a non-null skipped field.

[limits]
This analysis describes a historical conditional distribution, not a forecast. The engine's own validation states explicitly: "Analog retrieval hits its coverage target out of sample and its width tracks each instrument's own volatility, but it is NOT sharper than a same-name unconditional band at matched coverage, and its raw PIT distribution fails a uniformity test. It is a stress-testing and provenance instrument, not an alpha source." Specifically, the matched coverage sharpness versus the same-name unconditional benchmark is -3.4%, meaning the naive benchmark is tighter at the same coverage level. The raw PIT chi-square statistic is 363.9 against a 5% critical value of 16.92, confirming the failure of the uniformity test. The directional hit rate is only 54%. Only 1 of the 50 retrieved analogs is TSLA itself, so the distribution is built almost entirely from other names sharing similar feature geometry. Provenance relies on keyless price data from api.stockanalysis.com and earnings dates clustered via SEC full-text search, which introduces noise. Every stress scenario carries its own caveat, most notably that macro windows are sampled repeatedly due to date caps, and structural risks like delisting do not register in the feature space.
